observations.title: Fixed-bank frame loop and bank transitions
observed: CC1A waits at F2F7 and CC44 jumps back to CC1A.
D010 loads A=5 and tail-calls F2D3. CB00 loads A=2 and tail-calls F2D3.
CC20 calls bank5:861E; CC26 calls bank2:A4E8; CC2C calls bank5:8B04; CC32 calls bank5:80F9.
D8FC selects bank4 before CC38 calls BADF; CB00 selects bank2 before CC3E calls9F12, followed by CC41 calling A3DD.
interpretation: The engine coordinates per-frame subsystems across switchable banks using small fixed-bank wrappers.
unknowns: Most callee semantics, exact physics, combat AI and cycle timing are not recovered by this call inventory.
The imported bank5+7 image cannot establish bodies at the same addresses while banks2/4/6 are selected.
The bank at CC41 also depends on whether the preceding9F12 callee preserves its selected bank; that callee is not analyzed here.

observations.title: Bank switch helper preserves Y and records the selected bank
observed: Saves Y in RAM0041, copies A to Y, stores A in RAM06D1, writes A to FFF0+Y, restores Y and returns.
interpretation: For this mapper2 ROM, A is the selected16KiB PRG bank. FFF0..FFF7 contain the matching values0..7.

observations.title: Frame barrier uses a RAM flag written by the interrupt
observed: Stores0 to RAM040C and repeatedly reads it until nonzero before returning.
NMI FF CF loads6, selects bank6 at FFF6, and writes the same6 to RAM040C at FFD4.
interpretation: Main code waits for the next NMI completion phase; this is a frame synchronization barrier.
unknowns: This static observation does not measure actual frame rate, missed frames or cycle costs.

observations.title: NMI saves CPU state, updates video/input and releases the frame barrier
observed: Saves A/X/Y and writes0 to PPUMASK2001 at entry.
RAM04AC nonzero skips most updates and branches to FFCF.
If RAM0020 is nonzero, explicitly selects bank5 and calls884F.
Selects bank4 at FF37..FF39, then uses several RAM flags to choose update calls.
FF C4..FF CC explicitly selects bank5 and calls8AB7 then8344.
FF CF..FF D7 selects bank6, writes6 to040C and calls AA16.
Calls AA1C only when RAM0734 and04EB are both zero.
Calls EAE3, restores Y/X/A and returns with RTI at FFEF.
interpretation: The selected bank5 calls corroborate sprite DMA, video-register updates and controller polling during NMI.
unknowns: The FF13 entry required a separately seeded exact ROM slice; earlier callees are unmapped in that slice.
The semantics of several bank2/4/6 update routines and flags remain unknown.

observations.title: Two serial controller bytes, previous input and restricted intro controls
observed: When04D7 is zero, copies old040A to0037 and clears040A/040B.
When070C is nonzero, writes1 then0 to4016 and performs eight reads each from4016 and4017.
Each read's bit0 is rotated into040A or040B.
If0735 is nonzero and zero-page0051 equals2, masks040A with03.
NMI explicitly selects bank5 before its FFCC call to8344.
interpretation: 040A/040B are the two controller bitmasks and0037 retains previous player1 input.
Using standard NES serial order, bits7..0 are A,B,Select,Start,Up,Down,Left,Right.
The special0735/room-index2 condition permits Left/Right and suppresses other controls.
unknowns: The broader meanings of04D7 and070C are only known as polling gates here.

observations.title: Sprite attribute DMA uploads CPU page0200
observed: Initializes bytes0200..0203 to CE,FF,20,F6.
Reads2002, sets OAMADDR2003 to0 and writes2 to OAMDMA4014.
NMI selects bank5 before this call when0020 is nonzero.
interpretation: NES OAM DMA therefore copies256 sprite-attribute bytes from CPU0200..02FF.

observations.title: Cached rendering control and scroll values
observed: Writes RAM0014 to2000,0015 to2001,001B then001C to2005.
NMI explicitly selects bank5 before calling this routine.
interpretation: These bytes cache PPUCTRL, PPUMASK and horizontal/vertical scroll respectively.
unknowns: Ghidra's C pseudocode collapses the two writes to2005; the complete assembly retains both.

observations.title: A4096-byte PRG-to-PPU transfer
observed: Calls mapper helper F2D3, then writes X followed by0 to PPUADDR2006.
Performs16 iterations of256 reads from source pointer0017/0018 through Y, writing each byte to PPUDATA2007.
Increments source-pointer high byte0018 after each256-byte block.
Tail-calls D010, selecting bank5 before returning.
interpretation: The game can upload a4KiB pattern-table-sized block from banked PRG data into CHR-RAM.
unknowns: PPU address increment mode and the calling source pointer/bank must be established at each call site.
This function required a separately seeded exact ROM slice; lower callees are unmapped in that slice.

observations.title: Level-indexed room data pointer
observed: Calls C0D5; loads EB3A+X and EB3B+X into pointer006D/006E.
C0D5 is LDA0070; ASL; TAX; RTS, so X is twice the level index.
The EB3A table's original ROM file offset is1EB4A.
interpretation: Together with exact extraction boundaries, this corroborates the14 little-endian room-stream pointers.
unknowns: C0C7 itself does not select bank6; caller bank context is required before dereferencing006D/006E.

observations.title: Level-indexed spawn/guard/event header pointer
observed: Calls C0D5; loads EB56+X and EB57+X into pointer006D/006E.
The EB56 table's original ROM file offset is1EB66.
interpretation: This is the pointer table used by the separately recovered spawn and guard layouts.
unknowns: This helper also leaves bank selection to its caller.

observations.title: Guard-list initialization and an extra header read
observed: Sets0708=15hex, initializes scratch17/18 to0 and calls E0E1, which selects bank6.
For index RAM0018, reads header[index+3]&1F; values below30 produce a pair at0710+offset (room index) and0711+offset (position).
Increments output offset17 by2 per accepted pair; appends FF as list terminator.
The loop stops when0018 reaches19hex=25, so it performs25 reads with indices0..24.
Recovered format boundaries contain24 guard bytes; the final read overlaps the first event's source-room byte in all14 levels.
interpretation: The packed list records zero-based room indices and guard tile positions.
The extra entry has room index24, beyond actual room indices0..23; it may be unused by normal room lookups.
unknowns: No dynamic trace yet establishes the practical consequence of the extra entry; it is not evidence of a25th room.

observations.title: Five-entry fixed-bank state/mode dispatch table
observed: 8B04..8B12 doubles002C, loads target bytes from CB42+X/CB43+X into0017/0018, then JMP(0017).
The first five contiguous16-bit table entries are CC47,CC54,CC66,CCD6,CCEF; executable JSR CB00 starts at CB4C.
Main loop selects bank5 before its CC2C call to8B04.
interpretation: RAM002C acts as a mode/state selector for these fixed-bank handlers.
unknowns: Ghidra overextends this function through indirect targets, data and unavailable bank contexts.
Only the locally byte-validated8B04..8B12 assembly is accepted here. Its large pseudocode body is not recovered original source.
Specific state meanings and a complete list of valid runtime002C values remain unresolved.

observations.title: D4A2 selects level-data bank and restores working room/pointer state
observed: Calls E0E1 (select bank6), copies06CD/06CE into zero-page0C/0D and04DE into0051.
interpretation: This restores working pointer/room context. It is not the mapper write helper; F2D3 performs that write.
unknowns: The full provenance of06CD/06CE and04DE needs additional callers/value-flow analysis.

limitations: Static disassembly and data boundaries do not prove gameplay timing or full behavioral equivalence.
A single static8000-BFFF mapping cannot follow all bank changes; many Ghidra callee names/body boundaries are contextually invalid.
Original executable source, symbolic variable names, full collision rules, animation timing, guard AI, music and story scripts are not fully recovered.
The editable C/Wasm game is an independent implementation using recovered data; its physics/AI are not asserted to match these original routines.

graphics.scope: Focused static graphics analysis through Rea/Ghidra plus exact original-ROM data extraction; no ROM execution

observations.finding: E605 reads 16-bit graphics IDs through $5A, skips $0000, terminates at $FFFF, selects bank 3, and uploads 16-byte 2bpp tiles from $8000 + 16*ID to PPU $2007.
E0C4 indexes original layout pointer tables in bank 4: $8E26 when RAM $04BB = 0, or $8DEA otherwise. Each entry is indexed by 2*type.
E593 indexes graphics-list pointers in bank 2: $B0E9 when RAM $04BB = 0, or $B043 otherwise, using 2*type. E605 reads the pointed lists in bank 5.
E6CB draws 7 nametable columns for 10 rows minus layout-header row skips. A zero layout byte leaves the previous nametable tile unchanged; a nonzero byte adds the allocated CHR base.

observations.finding: The initializer at ROM $B81E sets PPU destination $1010 and allocation counter $76 = 0. Layout index 1 therefore names the first uploaded graphics word.

byte_anchor.method: raw byte anchor plus manual6502 decoding
byte_anchor.observation: LDA#$10; STA$72; STA$73; LDA#0; STA$75; STA$049A; STA$76. PPU destination$1010 and allocation counter0 prove layout index1 uses first loaded word.

observations.finding: E11D advances each logical horizontal cell by 4 nametable columns, or 32 pixels.
F32B reads word lists through $7B. Source bank is RAM $52 + (word >> 10), and source address is $8000 + 16*(word & 1023). It copies 16-byte tiles to PPU or RAM; full sprite framing remains unknown.
